subject: Civil Engineering
title: Supplementary Cementitious Materials
description: A 60-second lesson on Supplementary Cementitious Materials.

hook.text: Fly ash from coal plants and slag from steel mills — waste products that improve concrete.

buildup.text: Fly ash replaces 15-30% of cement. It reacts slowly with calcium hydroxide to add strength.

discovery.text: Slag cement replaces up to 70% of Portland cement — lighter color and better durability.

twist.text: Silica fume particles are 100 times smaller than cement — they fill microscopic pores.

climax.text: Using SCMs cuts cement demand, reduces CO₂, and makes the concrete denser and stronger.

punchline.text: Industrial waste becomes concrete's secret ingredient — cheaper and greener.

quiz.question: How does silica fume improve concrete?
options: It adds color to the concrete for decorative purposes
Its ultra-fine particles fill microscopic pores, increasing density and strength
It replaces water in the mix to reduce curing time
